content:
I've been working on a first attempt at synthesizing discussions about grind best practices into documentation: https://github.com/chenson2018/leanprover-community.github.io/blob/grind-style/templates/contribute/grind.md

This isn't exhaustive by any means (there's nothing about selecting good annotations for instance), but I thought I would go ahead and share to gather some feedback and potential additions. It seems like it would be good to have some documentation available sooner rather than later as grind usage increases in Mathlib.

A few comments to make it even more useful:

  • readability: if grind can be replaced by ring/linarith/omega/positivity/simp, I'd prefer these over grind: a grind proof is "clearly true and cannot be too difficult", but I know nothing how it actually worked. In contrast, positivity provides information what's actually happening.
  • I don't understand "it is similarly not preferred for the same reasons as simp." Is the point that we don't want terminal "grind only" (and grind is a closing tactic), so grind only is discouraged except for performance?
  • the "explicit unification" is a great trick I learned from you. I'm not sure if I'd understand it just from reading the writing --- can you add a brief example? (Even something partial would help: do apply foo; grind [bar] over grind [foo, bar])
And my meta-question: can we lint for these practices? :slight_smile:

For each point:

  • Mostly agreed, though I think #nightly-testing > nightly-testing regression log sends a bit of a mixed message. lia should be included in this too.
  • Yes, I mean exactly that grind only should be consider the same as terminal simp only.
  • I find it hard to include examples for grind, but the partial suggestion seems good.

For linting, we do now check grind? as I mention in the first section. I think of this as a hopefully temporary check that helps us give examples to core of this behavior. Squeezing grind could similarly be included as a follow-up to #36728 (which is waiting on me). For "Usage in Fundamental Modules", this could be a syntax linter if we'd like to strictly enforce it. Past that, I'm not sure.

My own meta question: where's the best place for this sort of documentation to live? The branch this is on adds a new file for the leanprover-community website because it felt a bit much to tack onto the style guide. I can open a draft PR or if a maintainer/Mathlib Initiative is already working on this sort of thing, I'm happy for them to adopt what seems most useful.

My 2 cents here are that grind is still relatively new to hope for a global consensus on best practices, so it might be a bit early to discuss integration inside the community webpage. On the other hand, the insights you gathered are extremely useful, so why not writing a post?
I would agree with this in principle --- at the same time, the insights listed appear quite basic and uncontroversial to me. (For others, posting them elsewhere to "incubate" is probably good.)

I'm mulling over best practices about being explicit with patterns. Consider these proofs of docs#List.countP_erase

import Batteries.Data.List.Perm
import Mathlib.Tactic.Common
import Batteries.Data.List.Lemmas

set_option linter.tacticAnalysis.verifyGrindOnly true

variable {α β : Type*} [BEq α] [LawfulBEq α] (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) (a : α)

namespace List

-- this is fine: `grind?` works as expected, as is probably what's intended
-- (it also appears to be a little faster)
example : countP p (l.erase a) = countP p l - if a ∈ l ∧ p a then 1 else 0 := by
  grind [= countP_eq_length_filter]

-- this is currently what's in Mathlib, `grind?` fails
example : countP p (l.erase a) = countP p l - if a ∈ l ∧ p a then 1 else 0 := by
  grind [countP_eq_length_filter]

-- I'm guessing it's treating `countP_eq_length_filter` as an arbitrary term, since this gives the same stable hashes
-- Note that `grind?` also works here! I don't know enough about `grind` internals to track down why
example : countP p (l.erase a) = countP p l - if a ∈ l ∧ p a then 1 else 0 := by
  grind [@countP_eq_length_filter α]

Given the potential for confusion, grind? behavior, and maybe performance, it seems like it's better to specify your grind patterns explicitly if it's otherwise interpreted as an arbitrary term.
